images.title: How long is a minute: two groups
images.purpose: Show the two dot plots of minute estimates, each with its mean and median lines, so the groups can be compared by spread and centre.
images.composition: Two dot plots stacked one above the other on the same scale from 40 to 75 seconds.
exact_structure: Top plot, First group: 33 teal (#0072B2) dots spread from 42 to 68 seconds, most of them stacked between 53 and 62, with a tallest stack of 4 at 60; a solid vertical line at 58.21 (mean) and a dashed vertical line at 60 (median).

Bottom plot, Second group: 28 purple (#CC79A7) dots spread from 47 to 71 seconds, most of them stacked between 55 and 62, with a tallest stack of 4 near 61; a solid vertical line at 59.29 (mean) and a dashed vertical line at 59.5 (median).
Both number lines have numbered ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70 and 75 and the caption Time (in seconds).
A key at the right: a short solid line labelled Mean and a short dashed line labelled Median.
rejection: the mean and median lines in the same style
images.takeaway: The second group's estimates sit a little closer to 60 seconds and the first group has more far low guesses.
images.description: Two dot plots of minute estimates for two groups, each with a mean line and a median line.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which group's dots crowd closer to 60 before comparing the summary numbers.

image_decisions.why: Comparing the two groups' spread needs the dot plots in view.
